decisions.context: Authorization needs a fraud score within tens of milliseconds, so scoring must complete in the transaction path. The score must be available before the authorization decision proceeds.
decisions.rationale: A synchronous call makes the score available before authorization; its added latency must fit within the stated tens-of-milliseconds budget.
consequences: Authorization depends on scoring response time.
The scoring path needs a strict latency budget.

decisions.context: The service must continue working during peaks while returning scores quickly. Stateless workers can be replicated to add inference capacity without coordinating per-transaction state.
decisions.rationale: Replicated workers provide a straightforward way to add inference capacity during peaks and avoid a single scoring host as the sole failure point.
consequences: Shared feature and model dependencies must also support peak load.

decisions.decision: Serve a pinned model version for each scoring request
decisions.context: Auditors need to identify the model version that produced each score. Recording the version with the score makes the inference result traceable across model updates.

alternatives.label: Fetch a model for every request

decisions.rationale: Keeping a known artifact available to each worker avoids a per-request model fetch and lets the service attach an explicit version to every result.
consequences: Rollouts must manage model versions across workers.

decisions.decision: Record the model version and feature values with each score
decisions.context: The brief requires later audit of both the model version and the features used. Persisting these alongside the score provides a record of the specific inference inputs.

alternatives.label: Persist score with model and feature snapshot
Persist score and model version only

chosen.label: Persist score with model and feature snapshot

decisions.rationale: The required audit trail names both the model version and features, so storing a feature snapshot with each score most directly supports later review.
consequences: Every score creates a durable record.
Feature retention and access controls need definition.
